A stored job has a stable job_id and one state: ready, leased, or done.

# Recorded local protocol

## Question and units

Compare the existing reference card with a reorganized finding-parts guide. Four volunteers, V1 through V4, each performed two lookup tasks. Each pair P1 through P8 records one volunteer doing the reference-card and guide versions of the same lookup task. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent people. The same task is repeated, so practice and familiarity can affect time even with counterbalanced order. Order was balanced within each volunteer as recorded in pairs.csv. This was not a randomized sample of all store volunteers.

## Captured fields

reference.csv and guide.csv have pair_id,seconds,correct,assisted. Seconds is a positive elapsed time. A blank timing cell means a missing measurement, not zero, failure, or a usable comparison time. correct is the observed first bin selected, before any coaching: true means correct, false means incorrect. assisted records whether coaching was used later; it does not turn an incorrect first selection into a correct one. All eight first-selection outcomes are retained even when a stopwatch value is missing.

Use only pairs with both positive times for the time comparison. Match records by pair_id, not row position. Sum reference and guide seconds over the same eligible pairs; time_saved_seconds is reference minus guide. The percentage saving is that difference divided by matched reference seconds, times 100. Also count faster, slower and tied eligible pairs. Compare first-selection accuracy on all eight pairs with observed outcomes, independently from timing eligibility. Do not impute missing timing.

## Machine-readable audit

Write audit/metrics.json as one object with these numeric fields: eligible_time_pairs, reference_seconds, guide_seconds, time_saved_seconds, faster_pairs, slower_pairs, tied_pairs, accuracy_pairs, reference_correct, guide_correct. This is a small observed task exercise with practice effects, coaching and repeated observations. It can inform a limited check. # Finding-parts guide evidence audit

## Decision

Recommend a limited, staffed next check before standardizing the reorganized guide. The current evidence does not support replacing the reference card on every shift. In this exercise, the guide took 800 seconds against 910 reference seconds on seven eligible task pairs: a saving of 110 seconds, or approximately 12.09%. It was faster on five pairs and slower on two. First-selection accuracy was equal: seven correct selections out of eight (87.5%) for each format.

These observations justify investigating the guide further, but they do not establish that the guide causes faster work or preserves accuracy in ordinary shifts. Four volunteers supplied the eight task pairs, tasks were repeated between formats, coaching occurred, and one guide time is missing. No later unattended shift, expanded study, or rollout is documented. The draft summary should not be used as written; a corrected replacement appears below.

## Scope and governing rules

Reviewed all ten supplied files: [README](../README.md), the [protocol](../study/protocol.md), [pair assignments](../evidence/pairs.csv), [reference records](../evidence/reference.csv), [guide records](../evidence/guide.csv), [capture notes](../evidence/capture-notes.md), [draft summary](../draft-summary.md), both [reference](../guides/reference-card.txt) and [reorganized](../guides/reorganized-guide.txt) guide texts, and the [structural checker](../tools/check-evidence.cjs). The protocol defines the calculations; the capture notes explain the missing time and the meaning of first-selection outcomes. The draft is an unchecked interpretation. The guide texts describe the lookup procedures and supply no additional outcome evidence.

Each pair represents one volunteer repeating the same lookup task with the two formats. Join records by `pair_id`. Use both times only when each is present and positive, with reference minus guide defining seconds saved. Divide the total saving by the reference total over those same eligible pairs. Count accuracy independently on every pair with recorded first-selection outcomes. Later assistance does not change an observed first selection. Do not impute timing.

The JSON companion, [metrics.json](metrics.json), contains exactly the ten numeric fields required by the protocol. Percentages and interpretation remain in this document.

## Reconciled observations

Positive savings mean the guide was faster. A missing time is not a zero. Correct/incorrect below describe the first bin selected, before later coaching.

| Pair | Volunteer | Task | First format | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Seconds saved | Reference first selection | Guide first selection | Later assistance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | V1 | find_patch | reference | 120 | 90 | 30 | correct | correct | none recorded |
| P2 | V1 | find_pump | guide | 100 | 95 | 5 | correct | correct | none recorded |
| P3 | V2 | find_cable | reference | 160 | 100 | 60 | incorrect | correct | reference |
| P4 | V2 | find_tube | guide | 80 | 75 | 5 | correct | correct | none recorded |
| P5 | V3 | find_brake | reference | 140 | 150 | -10 | correct | incorrect | guide |
| P6 | V3 | find_lamp | guide | 200 | 160 | 40 | correct | correct | reference |
| P7 | V4 | find_chain | reference | 150 | missing | excluded | correct | correct | guide |
| P8 | V4 | find_valve | guide | 110 | 130 | -20 | correct | correct | none recorded |

All three CSV files contain P1 through P8 exactly once. Each of V1 through V4 supplies two task pairs, with one reference-first and one guide-first pair. Thus order was balanced within each volunteer and four pairs used each order overall. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent volunteers or independent replications.

P7's guide stopwatch value was lost during export. The capture notes explicitly say no alternative time is available. Exclude both P7's 150 reference seconds and its absent guide seconds from the time comparison. Retain P7's two correct first selections and its guide assistance flag. Neither task order nor another volunteer's record supplies a replacement time.

The capture notes and CSV outcomes agree: P3's reference first selection and P5's guide first selection were wrong, and observers later coached those tasks. The CSVs also record assistance on P6 reference and P7 guide, both after correct first selections. Assistance therefore appears on two of eight records per format, covering four distinct pairs. A correct initial choice does not mean no help was needed later. The pack does not establish the effect of coaching on elapsed time or eventual independent completion. All pairs with two valid times remain in the required timing calculation, including assisted or initially incorrect attempts.

## Independent arithmetic

Eligible timing pairs: P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P8.

```text
Reference seconds = 120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910
Guide seconds     =  90 +  95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800
Seconds saved     = 910 - 800 = 110
Cross-check       = 30 + 5 + 60 + 5 - 10 + 40 - 20 = 110
Percentage saved  = (110 / 910) * 100 = 12.087912...%, reported as 12.09%
Faster pairs      = P1, P2, P3, P4, P6 = 5
Slower pairs      = P5, P8 = 2
Tied pairs        = 0
Direction check   = 5 + 2 + 0 = 7 eligible pairs
```

The percentage is the saving in matched total seconds divided by matched reference seconds. It is not an average of individual pair percentages. Summing all reference times gives 1,060 seconds, but that includes P7 and is not a valid denominator against seven recorded guide times. There is no basis in the matched calculation for the draft's 30% claim.

Accuracy uses all eight pairs, independently of stopwatch completeness:

| First-selection outcome | Pair IDs | Count |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Both formats correct | P1, P2, P4, P6, P7, P8 | 6 |
| Reference incorrect, guide correct | P3 | 1 |
| Reference correct, guide incorrect | P5 | 1 |
| Both formats incorrect | none | 0 |

Reference accuracy is `(6 + 1) / 8 = 7 / 8 = 87.5%`; guide accuracy is also `(6 + 1) / 8 = 7 / 8 = 87.5%`. The observed difference is zero percentage points. Coaching cannot convert the two incorrect first selections into correct first selections. Equal observed totals do not establish equivalent accuracy in ordinary work or a safety guarantee.

## Corrections to the draft

| Draft assertion | Reconciled finding and consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Eight independent volunteers | Four volunteers, each contributing two pairs. Repeated observations from a person cannot be counted as additional independent people. |
| All eight completed time pairs | Seven pairs have both positive times. P7 lacks its guide time; timing excludes P7 while accuracy retains it. |
| Faster in every pair | Faster on five eligible pairs, slower on P5 and P8, with no ties. P7 has no measured speed comparison. |
| Cut total lookup time by 30% | Matched totals are 910 reference seconds and 800 guide seconds, saving 110 seconds or approximately 12.09%. |
| Eight correct guide first selections versus seven reference | Both formats have seven correct first selections out of eight. P5 is the guide error; P3 is the reference error. There is no observed accuracy improvement. |
| Coaching did not affect any result | Assistance was recorded for reference P3/P6 and guide P5/P7. Its influence on elapsed time is not isolated. Assistance occurred later and cannot rewrite first-selection outcomes. |
| Replace the reference card for every shift immediately; no uncertainty | The observed staffed exercise supports a limited next check. It does not establish readiness for standardization across volunteers and shifts. |

## Uncertainty and decision limits

The timing gain is a description of the seven measured task pairs. Every person saw both formats for a repeated task, so familiarity may affect the second attempt. Balanced order helps address order concerns but cannot remove practice or coaching effects. After excluding P7, the eligible subset contains three reference-first pairs and four guide-first pairs. As a descriptive check, reference-first pairs total 420 reference versus 340 guide seconds (80 seconds saved); guide-first pairs total 490 versus 460 (30 seconds saved). These small, different task groups cannot isolate an order effect or establish a causal guide effect.

Four people in a single staffed exercise provide little evidence about variation across volunteers, tasks, or ordinary shifts. The sample was not randomized from all store volunteers. The missing P7 time means the full eight-pair time difference is unknown; the audit makes no assumption that its omission is harmless or that its time would resemble another pair. Recorded speed includes attempts with wrong initial choices and later help, so it cannot be read as a measure of accurate, unaided task completion.

The observed guide error on P5 and slower guide times on P5/P8 deserve attention, but the records do not identify a specific fault in the guide text or prove that the guide caused these outcomes. Both guide texts direct users to check the physical label and ask a helper if it is unclear; neither text demonstrates that those safeguards work reliably. There is no outcome evidence from an unattended or ordinary-work rollout. This audit supplies no population speed guarantee, proof of equal accuracy, safety guarantee, or independent replication. It does not attach a confidence interval or significance claim based on treating the eight pairs as independent people.

## Limited next check for the coordinator to plan

The coordinator can use these findings to plan a bounded, staffed check before any decision to standardize. Keep the reference card and a shift helper available. Include tasks that probe the wrong guide selection on P5 and the slower guide attempts on P5/P8, alongside ordinary lookup work. This is a recommendation for planning; no volunteers have been contacted and no further study or rollout has been started.

Before a next check, the coordinator should set its scope, time limit and acceptance criteria: acceptable first-selection accuracy, when a wrong-bin choice or repeated need for help should halt and prompt revision, and what useful speed improvement would justify adoption. The current protocol supplies no thresholds for those decisions; this audit does not invent or retrospectively apply them.

Record every first selection before help, log assistance separately, retain complete matched times with a clear timing endpoint, and document missing measurements. Account for repeated people and task familiarity when choosing tasks and order. A limited check should resolve whether the guide remains accurate and usable during ordinary work, whether helpers are still needed, and whether the apparent time benefit persists. Only then should the coordinator reassess standardization.

## Corrected summary suitable for the coordinator

> Four volunteers each completed two matched lookup tasks using the reference card and the reorganized guide. Seven of the eight task pairs had usable times in both formats. Across those seven pairs, the reference card took 910 seconds and the guide took 800 seconds, an observed saving of 110 seconds (about 12.09%). The guide was faster on five pairs and slower on two. Across all eight pairs, each format had seven correct first selections (87.5%). Coaching occurred on two records per format, and one guide time was missing. Repeated tasks, a small group and staffed conditions limit what these results establish about ordinary shifts. The evidence supports planning a limited, staffed next check before deciding whether to standardize the guide.

A separate Node.js calculation from the source records agreed with all ten metrics, including the separate timing and accuracy denominators. The explicit arithmetic and pair ledger above provide a further transparent cross-check.
- Parsed the completed JSON and checked its exact field set, finite numeric values, totals, counts and agreement with the independently computed metrics. Confirmed `faster_pairs + slower_pairs + tied_pairs = eligible_time_pairs`, P7's timing exclusion and accuracy retention, both incorrect first selections, and all four assistance flags.
- Compared SHA-256 hashes for all ten supplied files before and after the audit; all were unchanged. The only files added are `audit/findings.md` and `audit/metrics.json`. # Finding-parts guide evidence audit

## Decision

Recommend a limited, staffed next check before standardizing the reorganized guide. The current evidence does not support replacing the reference card on every shift. In this exercise, the guide took 800 seconds against 910 reference seconds on seven eligible task pairs: a saving of 110 seconds, or approximately 12.09%. It was faster on five pairs and slower on two. First-selection accuracy was equal: seven correct selections out of eight (87.5%) for each format.

These observations justify investigating the guide further, but they do not establish that the guide causes faster work or preserves accuracy in ordinary shifts. Four volunteers supplied the eight task pairs, tasks were repeated between formats, coaching occurred, and one guide time is missing. No later unattended shift, expanded study, or rollout is documented. The draft summary should not be used as written; a corrected replacement appears below.

## Scope and governing rules

Reviewed all ten supplied files: [README](../README.md), the [protocol](../study/protocol.md), [pair assignments](../evidence/pairs.csv), [reference records](../evidence/reference.csv), [guide records](../evidence/guide.csv), [capture notes](../evidence/capture-notes.md), [draft summary](../draft-summary.md), both [reference](../guides/reference-card.txt) and [reorganized](../guides/reorganized-guide.txt) guide texts, and the [structural checker](../tools/check-evidence.cjs). The protocol defines the calculations; the capture notes explain the missing time and the meaning of first-selection outcomes. The draft is an unchecked interpretation. The guide texts describe the lookup procedures and supply no additional outcome evidence.

Each pair represents one volunteer repeating the same lookup task with the two formats. Join records by `pair_id`. Use both times only when each is present and positive, with reference minus guide defining seconds saved. Divide the total saving by the reference total over those same eligible pairs. Count accuracy independently on every pair with recorded first-selection outcomes. Later assistance does not change an observed first selection. Do not impute timing.

The JSON companion, [metrics.json](metrics.json), contains exactly the ten numeric fields required by the protocol. Percentages and interpretation remain in this document.

## Reconciled observations

Positive savings mean the guide was faster. A missing time is not a zero. Correct/incorrect below describe the first bin selected, before later coaching.

| Pair | Volunteer | Task | First format | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Seconds saved | Reference first selection | Guide first selection | Later assistance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | V1 | find_patch | reference | 120 | 90 | 30 | correct | correct | none recorded |
| P2 | V1 | find_pump | guide | 100 | 95 | 5 | correct | correct | none recorded |
| P3 | V2 | find_cable | reference | 160 | 100 | 60 | incorrect | correct | reference |
| P4 | V2 | find_tube | guide | 80 | 75 | 5 | correct | correct | none recorded |
| P5 | V3 | find_brake | reference | 140 | 150 | -10 | correct | incorrect | guide |
| P6 | V3 | find_lamp | guide | 200 | 160 | 40 | correct | correct | reference |
| P7 | V4 | find_chain | reference | 150 | missing | excluded | correct | correct | guide |
| P8 | V4 | find_valve | guide | 110 | 130 | -20 | correct | correct | none recorded |

All three CSV files contain P1 through P8 exactly once. Each of V1 through V4 supplies two task pairs, with one reference-first and one guide-first pair. Thus order was balanced within each volunteer and four pairs used each order overall. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent volunteers or independent replications.

P7's guide stopwatch value was lost during export. The capture notes explicitly say no alternative time is available. Exclude both P7's 150 reference seconds and its absent guide seconds from the time comparison. Retain P7's two correct first selections and its guide assistance flag. Neither task order nor another volunteer's record supplies a replacement time.

The capture notes and CSV outcomes agree: P3's reference first selection and P5's guide first selection were wrong, and observers later coached those tasks. The CSVs also record assistance on P6 reference and P7 guide, both after correct first selections. Assistance therefore appears on two of eight records per format, covering four distinct pairs. A correct initial choice does not mean no help was needed later. The pack does not establish the effect of coaching on elapsed time or eventual independent completion. All pairs with two valid times remain in the required timing calculation, including assisted or initially incorrect attempts.

## Independent arithmetic

Eligible timing pairs: P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P8.

```text
Reference seconds = 120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910
Guide seconds     =  90 +  95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800
Seconds saved     = 910 - 800 = 110
Cross-check       = 30 + 5 + 60 + 5 - 10 + 40 - 20 = 110
Percentage saved  = (110 / 910) * 100 = 12.087912...%, reported as 12.09%
Faster pairs      = P1, P2, P3, P4, P6 = 5
Slower pairs      = P5, P8 = 2
Tied pairs        = 0
Direction check   = 5 + 2 + 0 = 7 eligible pairs
```

The percentage is the saving in matched total seconds divided by matched reference seconds. It is not an average of individual pair percentages. Summing all reference times gives 1,060 seconds, but that includes P7 and is not a valid denominator against seven recorded guide times. There is no basis in the matched calculation for the draft's 30% claim.

Accuracy uses all eight pairs, independently of stopwatch completeness:

| First-selection outcome | Pair IDs | Count |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Both formats correct | P1, P2, P4, P6, P7, P8 | 6 |
| Reference incorrect, guide correct | P3 | 1 |
| Reference correct, guide incorrect | P5 | 1 |
| Both formats incorrect | none | 0 |

Reference accuracy is `(6 + 1) / 8 = 7 / 8 = 87.5%`; guide accuracy is also `(6 + 1) / 8 = 7 / 8 = 87.5%`. The observed difference is zero percentage points. Coaching cannot convert the two incorrect first selections into correct first selections. Equal observed totals do not establish equivalent accuracy in ordinary work or a safety guarantee.

## Corrections to the draft

| Draft assertion | Reconciled finding and consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Eight independent volunteers | Four volunteers, each contributing two pairs. Repeated observations from a person cannot be counted as additional independent people. |
| All eight completed time pairs | Seven pairs have both positive times. P7 lacks its guide time; timing excludes P7 while accuracy retains it. |
| Faster in every pair | Faster on five eligible pairs, slower on P5 and P8, with no ties. P7 has no measured speed comparison. |
| Cut total lookup time by 30% | Matched totals are 910 reference seconds and 800 guide seconds, saving 110 seconds or approximately 12.09%. |
| Eight correct guide first selections versus seven reference | Both formats have seven correct first selections out of eight. P5 is the guide error; P3 is the reference error. There is no observed accuracy improvement. |
| Coaching did not affect any result | Assistance was recorded for reference P3/P6 and guide P5/P7. Its influence on elapsed time is not isolated. Assistance occurred later and cannot rewrite first-selection outcomes. |
| Replace the reference card for every shift immediately; no uncertainty | The observed staffed exercise supports a limited next check. It does not establish readiness for standardization across volunteers and shifts. |

## Uncertainty and decision limits

The timing gain is a description of the seven measured task pairs. Every person saw both formats for a repeated task, so familiarity may affect the second attempt. Balanced order helps address order concerns but cannot remove practice or coaching effects. After excluding P7, the eligible subset contains three reference-first pairs and four guide-first pairs. As a descriptive check, reference-first pairs total 420 reference versus 340 guide seconds (80 seconds saved); guide-first pairs total 490 versus 460 (30 seconds saved). These small, different task groups cannot isolate an order effect or establish a causal guide effect.

Four people in a single staffed exercise provide little evidence about variation across volunteers, tasks, or ordinary shifts. The sample was not randomized from all store volunteers. The missing P7 time means the full eight-pair time difference is unknown; the audit makes no assumption that its omission is harmless or that its time would resemble another pair. Recorded speed includes attempts with wrong initial choices and later help, so it cannot be read as a measure of accurate, unaided task completion.

The observed guide error on P5 and slower guide times on P5/P8 deserve attention, but the records do not identify a specific fault in the guide text or prove that the guide caused these outcomes. Both guide texts direct users to check the physical label and ask a helper if it is unclear; neither text demonstrates that those safeguards work reliably. There is no outcome evidence from an unattended or ordinary-work rollout. This audit supplies no population speed guarantee, proof of equal accuracy, safety guarantee, or independent replication. It does not attach a confidence interval or significance claim based on treating the eight pairs as independent people.

## Limited next check for the coordinator to plan

The coordinator can use these findings to plan a bounded, staffed check before any decision to standardize. Keep the reference card and a shift helper available. Include tasks that probe the wrong guide selection on P5 and the slower guide attempts on P5/P8, alongside ordinary lookup work. This is a recommendation for planning; no volunteers have been contacted and no further study or rollout has been started.

Before a next check, the coordinator should set its scope, time limit and acceptance criteria: acceptable first-selection accuracy, when a wrong-bin choice or repeated need for help should halt and prompt revision, and what useful speed improvement would justify adoption. The current protocol supplies no thresholds for those decisions; this audit does not invent or retrospectively apply them.

Record every first selection before help, log assistance separately, retain complete matched times with a clear timing endpoint, and document missing measurements. Account for repeated people and task familiarity when choosing tasks and order. A limited check should resolve whether the guide remains accurate and usable during ordinary work, whether helpers are still needed, and whether the apparent time benefit persists. Only then should the coordinator reassess standardization.

## Corrected summary suitable for the coordinator

> Four volunteers each completed two matched lookup tasks using the reference card and the reorganized guide. Seven of the eight task pairs had usable times in both formats. Across those seven pairs, the reference card took 910 seconds and the guide took 800 seconds, an observed saving of 110 seconds (about 12.09%). The guide was faster on five pairs and slower on two. Across all eight pairs, each format had seven correct first selections (87.5%). Coaching occurred on two records per format, and one guide time was missing. Repeated tasks, a small group and staffed conditions limit what these results establish about ordinary shifts. The evidence supports planning a limited, staffed next check before deciding whether to standardize the guide.

## Verification and source preservation

- Ran `node tools/check-evidence.cjs` successfully with installed Node.js v25.0.0. It reported eight pair IDs, four volunteers, eight reference rows, eight guide rows and P7 as the only missing guide time. The checker verifies structure; its success does not validate the draft's benefit claims.

A separate Node.js calculation from the source records agreed with all ten metrics, including the separate timing and accuracy denominators. The explicit arithmetic and pair ledger above provide a further transparent cross-check.
- Parsed the completed JSON and checked its exact field set, finite numeric values, totals, counts and agreement with the independently computed metrics. Confirmed `faster_pairs + slower_pairs + tied_pairs = eligible_time_pairs`, P7's timing exclusion and accuracy retention, both incorrect first selections, and all four assistance flags.
- Compared SHA-256 hashes for all ten supplied files before and after the audit; all were unchanged. The only files added are `audit/findings.md` and `audit/metrics.json`. All work used this local pack and installed tools, with no external sources, services, other projects, participant contact or new study.

# Finding-parts guide study audit

## Decision

The supplied evidence supports a limited, staffed next check, not standardizing the reorganized guide now. The guide took less total time on the seven eligible task pairs, but first-selection accuracy was unchanged, two timed pairs were slower, and the exercise involved only four volunteers repeating tasks with staff available. The draft summary needs correction before use.

Suggested replacement summary:

> Four volunteers each compared both formats on two lookup tasks, producing eight task pairs. Seven pairs had both stopwatch values: the reference card totaled 910 seconds and the guide 800 seconds, a saving of 110 seconds (12.1% of matched reference time). The guide was faster in five pairs and slower in two. Both formats had seven correct first selections out of eight (87.5%); each had a different incorrect selection followed by coaching. Assistance was recorded in two trials per format. These descriptive results support a limited, staffed check of accuracy and usability in ordinary work before considering standardization. Repeated tasks, practice, assistance, missing timing and the small nonrandom group limit generalization.

## Sources and controlling rules

Reviewed all ten supplied files: [protocol](../study/protocol.md), [pair metadata](../evidence/pairs.csv), [reference records](../evidence/reference.csv), [guide records](../evidence/guide.csv), [capture notes](../evidence/capture-notes.md), [draft summary](../draft-summary.md), [README](../README.md), both [reference](../guides/reference-card.txt) and [reorganized](../guides/reorganized-guide.txt) guide texts, and the [structural checker](../tools/check-evidence.cjs). The guide texts provide procedural context, not additional observations or evidence of effectiveness. Both tell users to check the bin label and seek a helper when unclear.

The recorded protocol controls eligibility and definitions; the capture notes explain the missing measurement and first-selection errors. The draft is explicitly unverified historical input. Its conflicting claims do not override the records.

Records were joined by `pair_id`, with unique, matching P1–P8 IDs across the three CSVs. Timing uses only pairs with two positive measurements. A blank is missing, not zero or failure. Accuracy uses all eight observed first selections, independently of timing. Later assistance does not change a first-selection outcome. Assisted timed pairs remain in the primary calculation because the protocol does not exclude them.

## Reconciled timing records

Positive savings mean the guide was faster. Times are seconds. “First format” comes from `pairs.csv`.

| Pair | Volunteer | Task | First format | Reference | Guide | Reference minus guide |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| P1 | V1 | find_patch | Reference | 120 | 90 | 30 |
| P2 | V1 | find_pump | Guide | 100 | 95 | 5 |
| P3 | V2 | find_cable | Reference | 160 | 100 | 60 |
| P4 | V2 | find_tube | Guide | 80 | 75 | 5 |
| P5 | V3 | find_brake | Reference | 140 | 150 | -10 |
| P6 | V3 | find_lamp | Guide | 200 | 160 | 40 |
| P7 | V4 | find_chain | Reference | 150 | Missing | Not eligible |
| P8 | V4 | find_valve | Guide | 110 | 130 | -20 |
| **Eligible total** | | | | **910** | **800** | **110** |

P7's guide stopwatch entry was lost during export. The notes explicitly state that no other timing exists in the pack. Both P7's recorded reference time of 150 seconds and its missing guide time are excluded from the time comparison. No seconds were reconstructed or imputed. Comparing all eight reference times against seven guide times would use different task sets and violate the protocol.

Independent arithmetic:

- Reference: `120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910` seconds.
- Guide: `90 + 95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800` seconds.
- Saving: `910 - 800 = 110` seconds, also `30 + 5 + 60 + 5 - 10 + 40 - 20 = 110`.
- Percentage saving: `100 * 110 / 910 = 12.087912...%`, reported as **12.1%**. This is the percentage reduction in matched aggregate time, not an average of pair percentages or a prediction for each volunteer.
- Faster: P1, P2, P3, P4, P6 (**5**); slower: P5, P8 (**2**); tied: **0**. These counts sum to seven eligible pairs.

## Reconciled accuracy and assistance

“Correct” refers to the first bin selected before coaching. Assistance is the separate later-help flag.

| Pair | Reference first selection | Reference assisted | Guide first selection | Guide assisted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Correct | No | Correct | No |
| P2 | Correct | No | Correct | No |
| P3 | Incorrect | Yes | Correct | No |
| P4 | Correct | No | Correct | No |
| P5 | Correct | No | Incorrect | Yes |
| P6 | Correct | Yes | Correct | No |
| P7 | Correct | No | Correct | Yes |
| P8 | Correct | No | Correct | No |

Reference accuracy is **7/8 = 87.5%**; guide accuracy is **7/8 = 87.5%**. The observed difference is **0 percentage points**. Six pairs were correct under both formats; P3 favored the guide and P5 favored the reference; none were incorrect under both. Equal totals do not establish equivalence, absence of harm, or a safety guarantee.

P3's reference error and P5's guide error agree with the capture notes and remain errors despite later coaching. P7 retains its correct guide first selection and its assistance flag even though its timing is missing. P6 also has a correct reference first selection with later assistance. Correct first selection and later help are compatible observations.

Reference assistance occurred on P3 and P6; guide assistance on P5 and P7: **2/8 trials per format**. Four of the eight task pairs had assistance in at least one format. The pack does not isolate coaching's effect on elapsed time, eventual completion, or later repeated-task performance. Equal assistance counts cannot substantiate the draft's claim that coaching affected no result.

## Corrections to the draft

| Draft claim | Audited correction |
| --- | --- |
| Eight independent volunteers | Four volunteers, V1–V4, each contributed two task pairs. The eight pairs are repeated observations, not eight independent people or replications. |
| All eight completed time pairs | Seven usable time pairs. P7 is missing its guide time; the pack does not support a claim about its paired duration. |
| Faster in every pair | Faster in five eligible pairs, slower in P5 and P8; P7 cannot be classified by time. |
| Total lookup time cut by 30% | The protocol calculation gives 110/910 = 12.1%. The 30% claim is unsupported. |
| Guide eight correct versus reference seven; accuracy improved | Both are seven correct first selections out of eight. P5's guide first selection was incorrect. No observed aggregate accuracy improvement. |
| Coaching did not affect any result | Assistance occurred in both formats. Its effect was not isolated; first-selection outcomes must remain as observed. |
| Replace the card for every shift immediately; no uncertainty | The small staffed exercise supports further limited checking. It does not establish ordinary-work accuracy and usability, universal speed or safety, or independent replication. |

The supplied draft has been left unchanged. Use the corrected text above in its place.

## Uncertainty and supporting descriptions

Each volunteer did one reference-first and one guide-first pair, so recorded order was balanced within every volunteer and across all eight pairs (four first in each format). Counterbalancing does not remove familiarity from repeating the same lookup task. Excluding P7 leaves only three reference-first and four guide-first timed pairs.

These optional breakdowns describe the same observations; they are not replacement primary analyses or independent confirmations:

| Timed subset | Pairs | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Saved seconds | Saving relative to subset reference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Reference first: P1, P3, P5 | 3 | 420 | 340 | 80 | 19.0% |
| Guide first: P2, P4, P6, P8 | 4 | 490 | 460 | 30 | 6.1% |
| Neither format assisted: P1, P2, P4, P8 | 4 | 410 | 390 | 20 | 4.9% |

The different order-group savings do not identify a practice effect because people and tasks also differ. Removing assisted pairs changes the task mix, so the unassisted subset cannot measure coaching's causal effect or replace the protocol result. It does show that the overall 12.1% saving should not be presented as a demonstrated independent-use benefit.

By volunteer, eligible savings were V1: 35 seconds across two pairs; V2: 65 across two; V3: 30 across two; V4: -20 across one. The missing P7 measurement leaves V4 represented by only P8 in timing. Neither the direction of the missing duration nor its impact on the complete eight-pair result is known.

This was a nonrandom group of four people in one staffed exercise. Task pairs share volunteers, and the same tasks were repeated under both formats. The aggregate favors the guide locally but does not separate format, practice, task and staff effects. No population confidence interval or significance claim is asserted here; treating seven timed pairs as seven independent people would misstate the evidence. There is no observed later unattended shift, expanded study or live rollout in the pack. Long-term usability, performance across ordinary shifts, and safety have not been established.

## Limited next check: decision for the coordinator

Before scheduling anything, define a bounded staffed check and agree on acceptable first-selection accuracy, usability, assistance and timing criteria. The current protocol supplies no numeric adoption threshold; this audit does not invent one. Keep the reference available while considering a trial. Examine the brake lookup associated with P5's incorrect guide selection and the valve lookup associated with P8's slowdown; their causes are not recorded, so neither can yet be attributed to a guide defect.

A proposed check should use representative ordinary-work lookups, reduce same-task practice with fresh or comparable tasks, and record order, volunteer identity, complete matched times, first selections before help, later assistance and observed confusion separately. Preserve bin-label verification and access to a helper. Review errors and usability problems before widening use. Assess whether any speed benefit persists alongside acceptable accuracy and manageable assistance, accounting for repeated observations per person. Any later standardization decision needs that ordinary-work evidence.

No additional input is needed to finish this audit. P7's missing stopwatch value remains unresolved and cannot be recovered from the supplied pack. The coordinator's outstanding decision is the scope and acceptance criteria of a limited next check. This is a recommendation only; no volunteers were contacted and no check or rollout was started.

## Verification and source preservation

- Ran `node tools/check-evidence.cjs`: passed; eight pairs, four volunteers, eight rows per format, and P7 as the only missing guide time. This tool checks structure and does not validate benefit claims.
- Independently parsed all three CSVs with a read-only Node script, joined on `pair_id`, checked positive finite observed times and boolean fields, and recalculated eligibility, totals, directional counts, accuracy, assistance, order balance and the descriptive breakdowns above. Its primary results match the explicit arithmetic in this report.
- Separately recalculated the required metrics with PowerShell `Import-Csv`, using ID-based lookups and explicit handling of blank times, then compared every result with `metrics.json`. Checked that the JSON contains exactly the ten required numeric fields, with no percentage or additional fields, and that count and time identities hold. All checks passed.
- Recorded SHA-256 hashes of all ten supplied files before writing the audit and compared them after writing. All supplied files are unchanged. Only `audit/findings.md` and `audit/metrics.json` were added. No external services or other projects were used.

The machine-readable result is [metrics.json](metrics.json). Percentages and interpretation remain in this report, as required by the protocol.

# Recorded local protocol

## Question and units

Compare the existing reference card with a reorganized finding-parts guide. Four volunteers, V1 through V4, each performed two lookup tasks. Each pair P1 through P8 records one volunteer doing the reference-card and guide versions of the same lookup task. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent people. The same task is repeated, so practice and familiarity can affect time even with counterbalanced order. Order was balanced within each volunteer as recorded in pairs.csv. This was not a randomized sample of all store volunteers.

## Captured fields

reference.csv and guide.csv have pair_id,seconds,correct,assisted. Seconds is a positive elapsed time. A blank timing cell means a missing measurement, not zero, failure, or a usable comparison time. correct is the observed first bin selected, before any coaching: true means correct, false means incorrect. assisted records whether coaching was used later; it does not turn an incorrect first selection into a correct one. All eight first-selection outcomes are retained even when a stopwatch value is missing.

Use only pairs with both positive times for the time comparison. Match records by pair_id, not row position. Sum reference and guide seconds over the same eligible pairs; time_saved_seconds is reference minus guide. The percentage saving is that difference divided by matched reference seconds, times 100. Also count faster, slower and tied eligible pairs. Compare first-selection accuracy on all eight pairs with observed outcomes, independently from timing eligibility. Do not impute missing timing.

## Machine-readable audit

Write audit/metrics.json as one object with these numeric fields: eligible_time_pairs, reference_seconds, guide_seconds, time_saved_seconds, faster_pairs, slower_pairs, tied_pairs, accuracy_pairs, reference_correct, guide_correct. Use the recorded rules above. Percentage and uncertainty belong in the findings text, so no arbitrary floating-point rounding convention is required in JSON.

## Interpretation

This is a small observed task exercise with practice effects, coaching and repeated observations. It can inform a limited check. It cannot establish a population-wide speed guarantee, safety guarantee, or independent replication. Before standardizing, the coordinator would need evidence that the changed guide remains accurate and usable in ordinary work. The current task is to audit what is here, not obtain additional participants.

# Finding-parts guide study audit

## Decision

The supplied evidence supports a limited, staffed next check, not standardizing the reorganized guide now. The guide took less total time on the seven eligible task pairs, but first-selection accuracy was unchanged, two timed pairs were slower, and the exercise involved only four volunteers repeating tasks with staff available. The draft summary needs correction before use.

Suggested replacement summary:

> Four volunteers each compared both formats on two lookup tasks, producing eight task pairs. Seven pairs had both stopwatch values: the reference card totaled 910 seconds and the guide 800 seconds, a saving of 110 seconds (12.1% of matched reference time). The guide was faster in five pairs and slower in two. Both formats had seven correct first selections out of eight (87.5%); each had a different incorrect selection followed by coaching. Assistance was recorded in two trials per format. These descriptive results support a limited, staffed check of accuracy and usability in ordinary work before considering standardization. Repeated tasks, practice, assistance, missing timing and the small nonrandom group limit generalization.

## Sources and controlling rules

Reviewed all ten supplied files: [protocol](../study/protocol.md), [pair metadata](../evidence/pairs.csv), [reference records](../evidence/reference.csv), [guide records](../evidence/guide.csv), [capture notes](../evidence/capture-notes.md), [draft summary](../draft-summary.md), [README](../README.md), both [reference](../guides/reference-card.txt) and [reorganized](../guides/reorganized-guide.txt) guide texts, and the [structural checker](../tools/check-evidence.cjs). The guide texts provide procedural context, not additional observations or evidence of effectiveness. Both tell users to check the bin label and seek a helper when unclear.

The recorded protocol controls eligibility and definitions; the capture notes explain the missing measurement and first-selection errors. The draft is explicitly unverified historical input. Its conflicting claims do not override the records.

Records were joined by `pair_id`, with unique, matching P1–P8 IDs across the three CSVs. Timing uses only pairs with two positive measurements. A blank is missing, not zero or failure. Accuracy uses all eight observed first selections, independently of timing. Later assistance does not change a first-selection outcome. Assisted timed pairs remain in the primary calculation because the protocol does not exclude them.

## Reconciled timing records

Positive savings mean the guide was faster. Times are seconds. “First format” comes from `pairs.csv`.

| Pair | Volunteer | Task | First format | Reference | Guide | Reference minus guide |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| P1 | V1 | find_patch | Reference | 120 | 90 | 30 |
| P2 | V1 | find_pump | Guide | 100 | 95 | 5 |
| P3 | V2 | find_cable | Reference | 160 | 100 | 60 |
| P4 | V2 | find_tube | Guide | 80 | 75 | 5 |
| P5 | V3 | find_brake | Reference | 140 | 150 | -10 |
| P6 | V3 | find_lamp | Guide | 200 | 160 | 40 |
| P7 | V4 | find_chain | Reference | 150 | Missing | Not eligible |
| P8 | V4 | find_valve | Guide | 110 | 130 | -20 |
| **Eligible total** | | | | **910** | **800** | **110** |

P7's guide stopwatch entry was lost during export. The notes explicitly state that no other timing exists in the pack. Both P7's recorded reference time of 150 seconds and its missing guide time are excluded from the time comparison. No seconds were reconstructed or imputed. Comparing all eight reference times against seven guide times would use different task sets and violate the protocol.

Independent arithmetic:

- Reference: `120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910` seconds.
- Guide: `90 + 95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800` seconds.
- Saving: `910 - 800 = 110` seconds, also `30 + 5 + 60 + 5 - 10 + 40 - 20 = 110`.
- Percentage saving: `100 * 110 / 910 = 12.087912...%`, reported as **12.1%**. This is the percentage reduction in matched aggregate time, not an average of pair percentages or a prediction for each volunteer.
- Faster: P1, P2, P3, P4, P6 (**5**); slower: P5, P8 (**2**); tied: **0**. These counts sum to seven eligible pairs.

## Reconciled accuracy and assistance

“Correct” refers to the first bin selected before coaching. Assistance is the separate later-help flag.

| Pair | Reference first selection | Reference assisted | Guide first selection | Guide assisted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Correct | No | Correct | No |
| P2 | Correct | No | Correct | No |
| P3 | Incorrect | Yes | Correct | No |
| P4 | Correct | No | Correct | No |
| P5 | Correct | No | Incorrect | Yes |
| P6 | Correct | Yes | Correct | No |
| P7 | Correct | No | Correct | Yes |
| P8 | Correct | No | Correct | No |

Reference accuracy is **7/8 = 87.5%**; guide accuracy is **7/8 = 87.5%**. The observed difference is **0 percentage points**. Six pairs were correct under both formats; P3 favored the guide and P5 favored the reference; none were incorrect under both. Equal totals do not establish equivalence, absence of harm, or a safety guarantee.

P3's reference error and P5's guide error agree with the capture notes and remain errors despite later coaching. P7 retains its correct guide first selection and its assistance flag even though its timing is missing. P6 also has a correct reference first selection with later assistance. Correct first selection and later help are compatible observations.

Reference assistance occurred on P3 and P6; guide assistance on P5 and P7: **2/8 trials per format**. Four of the eight task pairs had assistance in at least one format. The pack does not isolate coaching's effect on elapsed time, eventual completion, or later repeated-task performance. Equal assistance counts cannot substantiate the draft's claim that coaching affected no result.

## Corrections to the draft

| Draft claim | Audited correction |
| --- | --- |
| Eight independent volunteers | Four volunteers, V1–V4, each contributed two task pairs. The eight pairs are repeated observations, not eight independent people or replications. |
| All eight completed time pairs | Seven usable time pairs. P7 is missing its guide time; the pack does not support a claim about its paired duration. |
| Faster in every pair | Faster in five eligible pairs, slower in P5 and P8; P7 cannot be classified by time. |
| Total lookup time cut by 30% | The protocol calculation gives 110/910 = 12.1%. The 30% claim is unsupported. |
| Guide eight correct versus reference seven; accuracy improved | Both are seven correct first selections out of eight. P5's guide first selection was incorrect. No observed aggregate accuracy improvement. |
| Coaching did not affect any result | Assistance occurred in both formats. Its effect was not isolated; first-selection outcomes must remain as observed. |
| Replace the card for every shift immediately; no uncertainty | The small staffed exercise supports further limited checking. It does not establish ordinary-work accuracy and usability, universal speed or safety, or independent replication. |

The supplied draft has been left unchanged. Use the corrected text above in its place.

## Uncertainty and supporting descriptions

Each volunteer did one reference-first and one guide-first pair, so recorded order was balanced within every volunteer and across all eight pairs (four first in each format). Counterbalancing does not remove familiarity from repeating the same lookup task. Excluding P7 leaves only three reference-first and four guide-first timed pairs.

These optional breakdowns describe the same observations; they are not replacement primary analyses or independent confirmations:

| Timed subset | Pairs | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Saved seconds | Saving relative to subset reference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Reference first: P1, P3, P5 | 3 | 420 | 340 | 80 | 19.0% |
| Guide first: P2, P4, P6, P8 | 4 | 490 | 460 | 30 | 6.1% |
| Neither format assisted: P1, P2, P4, P8 | 4 | 410 | 390 | 20 | 4.9% |

The different order-group savings do not identify a practice effect because people and tasks also differ. Removing assisted pairs changes the task mix, so the unassisted subset cannot measure coaching's causal effect or replace the protocol result. It does show that the overall 12.1% saving should not be presented as a demonstrated independent-use benefit.

By volunteer, eligible savings were V1: 35 seconds across two pairs; V2: 65 across two; V3: 30 across two; V4: -20 across one. The missing P7 measurement leaves V4 represented by only P8 in timing. Neither the direction of the missing duration nor its impact on the complete eight-pair result is known.

This was a nonrandom group of four people in one staffed exercise. Task pairs share volunteers, and the same tasks were repeated under both formats. The aggregate favors the guide locally but does not separate format, practice, task and staff effects. No population confidence interval or significance claim is asserted here; treating seven timed pairs as seven independent people would misstate the evidence. There is no observed later unattended shift, expanded study or live rollout in the pack. Long-term usability, performance across ordinary shifts, and safety have not been established.

## Limited next check: decision for the coordinator

Before scheduling anything, define a bounded staffed check and agree on acceptable first-selection accuracy, usability, assistance and timing criteria. The current protocol supplies no numeric adoption threshold; this audit does not invent one. Keep the reference available while considering a trial. Examine the brake lookup associated with P5's incorrect guide selection and the valve lookup associated with P8's slowdown; their causes are not recorded, so neither can yet be attributed to a guide defect.

A proposed check should use representative ordinary-work lookups, reduce same-task practice with fresh or comparable tasks, and record order, volunteer identity, complete matched times, first selections before help, later assistance and observed confusion separately. Preserve bin-label verification and access to a helper. Review errors and usability problems before widening use. Assess whether any speed benefit persists alongside acceptable accuracy and manageable assistance, accounting for repeated observations per person. Any later standardization decision needs that ordinary-work evidence.

No additional input is needed to finish this audit. P7's missing stopwatch value remains unresolved and cannot be recovered from the supplied pack. The coordinator's outstanding decision is the scope and acceptance criteria of a limited next check. This is a recommendation only; no volunteers were contacted and no check or rollout was started.

## Verification and source preservation

- Ran `node tools/check-evidence.cjs`: passed; eight pairs, four volunteers, eight rows per format, and P7 as the only missing guide time. This tool checks structure and does not validate benefit claims.
- Independently parsed all three CSVs with a read-only Node script, joined on `pair_id`, checked positive finite observed times and boolean fields, and recalculated eligibility, totals, directional counts, accuracy, assistance, order balance and the descriptive breakdowns above. Its primary results match the explicit arithmetic in this report.
- Separately recalculated the required metrics with PowerShell `Import-Csv`, using ID-based lookups and explicit handling of blank times, then compared every result with `metrics.json`. Checked that the JSON contains exactly the ten required numeric fields, with no percentage or additional fields, and that count and time identities hold. All checks passed.
- Recorded SHA-256 hashes of all ten supplied files before writing the audit and compared them after writing. All supplied files are unchanged. Only `audit/findings.md` and `audit/metrics.json` were added. No external services or other projects were used.

The machine-readable result is [metrics.json](metrics.json). Percentages and interpretation remain in this report, as required by the protocol.

# Finding-parts guide study audit

## Decision

The supplied evidence supports a limited, staffed next check, not standardizing the reorganized guide now. The guide took less total time on the seven eligible task pairs, but first-selection accuracy was unchanged, two timed pairs were slower, and the exercise involved only four volunteers repeating tasks with staff available. The draft summary needs correction before use.

Suggested replacement summary:

> Four volunteers each compared both formats on two lookup tasks, producing eight task pairs. Seven pairs had both stopwatch values: the reference card totaled 910 seconds and the guide 800 seconds, a saving of 110 seconds (12.1% of matched reference time). The guide was faster in five pairs and slower in two. Both formats had seven correct first selections out of eight (87.5%); each had a different incorrect selection followed by coaching. Assistance was recorded in two trials per format. These descriptive results support a limited, staffed check of accuracy and usability in ordinary work before considering standardization. Repeated tasks, practice, assistance, missing timing and the small nonrandom group limit generalization.

## Sources and controlling rules

Reviewed all ten supplied files: [protocol](../study/protocol.md), [pair metadata](../evidence/pairs.csv), [reference records](../evidence/reference.csv), [guide records](../evidence/guide.csv), [capture notes](../evidence/capture-notes.md), [draft summary](../draft-summary.md), [README](../README.md), both [reference](../guides/reference-card.txt) and [reorganized](../guides/reorganized-guide.txt) guide texts, and the [structural checker](../tools/check-evidence.cjs). The guide texts provide procedural context, not additional observations or evidence of effectiveness. Both tell users to check the bin label and seek a helper when unclear.

The recorded protocol controls eligibility and definitions; the capture notes explain the missing measurement and first-selection errors. The draft is explicitly unverified historical input. Its conflicting claims do not override the records.

Records were joined by `pair_id`, with unique, matching P1–P8 IDs across the three CSVs. Timing uses only pairs with two positive measurements. A blank is missing, not zero or failure. Accuracy uses all eight observed first selections, independently of timing. Later assistance does not change a first-selection outcome. Assisted timed pairs remain in the primary calculation because the protocol does not exclude them.

## Reconciled timing records

Positive savings mean the guide was faster. Times are seconds. “First format” comes from `pairs.csv`.

| Pair | Volunteer | Task | First format | Reference | Guide | Reference minus guide |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| P1 | V1 | find_patch | Reference | 120 | 90 | 30 |
| P2 | V1 | find_pump | Guide | 100 | 95 | 5 |
| P3 | V2 | find_cable | Reference | 160 | 100 | 60 |

Comparing all eight reference times against seven guide times would use different task sets and violate the protocol.

Independent arithmetic:

- Reference: `120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910` seconds.
- Guide: `90 + 95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800` seconds.
- Saving: `910 - 800 = 110` seconds, also `30 + 5 + 60 + 5 - 10 + 40 - 20 = 110`.
- Percentage saving: `100 * 110 / 910 = 12.087912...%`, reported as **12.1%**. This is the percentage reduction in matched aggregate time, not an average of pair percentages or a prediction for each volunteer.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Correct | No | Correct | No |
| P2 | Correct | No | Correct | No |

Reference accuracy is **7/8 = 87.5%**; guide accuracy is **7/8 = 87.5%**. The observed difference is **0 percentage points**. Six pairs were correct under both formats; P3 favored the guide and P5 favored the reference; none were incorrect under both. Equal totals do not establish equivalence, absence of harm, or a safety guarantee.

P3's reference error and P5's guide error agree with the capture notes and remain errors despite later coaching. P7 retains its correct guide first selection and its assistance flag even though its timing is missing. P6 also has a correct reference first selection with later assistance. Correct first selection and later help are compatible observations.

Reference assistance occurred on P3 and P6; guide assistance on P5 and P7: **2/8 trials per format**. Four of the eight task pairs had assistance in at least one format. | Draft claim | Audited correction |
| --- | --- |
| Eight independent volunteers | Four volunteers, V1–V4, each contributed two task pairs. The eight pairs are repeated observations, not eight independent people or replications. |
| All eight completed time pairs | Seven usable time pairs. P7 is missing its guide time; the pack does not support a claim about its paired duration. |
| Faster in every pair | Faster in five eligible pairs, slower in P5 and P8; P7 cannot be classified by time. |
| Total lookup time cut by 30% | The protocol calculation gives 110/910 = 12.1%. The 30% claim is unsupported. |
| Guide eight correct versus reference seven; accuracy improved | Both are seven correct first selections out of eight. P5's guide first selection was incorrect. No observed aggregate accuracy improvement. |
| Coaching did not affect any result | Assistance occurred in both formats. Its effect was not isolated; first-selection outcomes must remain as observed. |
| Replace the card for every shift immediately; no uncertainty | The small staffed exercise supports further limited checking. It does not establish ordinary-work accuracy and usability, universal speed or safety, or independent replication. |

The supplied draft has been left unchanged. Use the corrected text above in its place.

## Uncertainty and supporting descriptions

Each volunteer did one reference-first and one guide-first pair, so recorded order was balanced within every volunteer and across all eight pairs (four first in each format). Counterbalancing does not remove familiarity from repeating the same lookup task. Excluding P7 leaves only three reference-first and four guide-first timed pairs.

These optional breakdowns describe the same observations; they are not replacement primary analyses or independent confirmations:

| Timed subset | Pairs | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Saved seconds | Saving relative to subset reference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Reference first: P1, P3, P5 | 3 | 420 | 340 | 80 | 19.0% |
| Guide first: P2, P4, P6, P8 | 4 | 490 | 460 | 30 | 6.1% |
| Neither format assisted: P1, P2, P4, P8 | 4 | 410 | 390 | 20 | 4.9% |

The different order-group savings do not identify a practice effect because people and tasks also differ. Removing assisted pairs changes the task mix, so the unassisted subset cannot measure coaching's causal effect or replace the protocol result. It does show that the overall 12.1% saving should not be presented as a demonstrated independent-use benefit.

By volunteer, eligible savings were V1: 35 seconds across two pairs; V2: 65 across two; V3: 30 across two; V4: -20 across one. The missing P7 measurement leaves V4 represented by only P8 in timing. Neither the direction of the missing duration nor its impact on the complete eight-pair result is known.

This was a nonrandom group of four people in one staffed exercise. Task pairs share volunteers, and the same tasks were repeated under both formats. The aggregate favors the guide locally but does not separate format, practice, task and staff effects. No population confidence interval or significance claim is asserted here; treating seven timed pairs as seven independent people would misstate the evidence. There is no observed later unattended shift, expanded study or live rollout in the pack. Long-term usability, performance across ordinary shifts, and safety have not been established.

The volunteer repair store is considering a reorganized guide for finding parts. The coordinator has a draft summary and wants an evidence check before making it the standard guide for everyone. # Recorded local protocol

## Question and units

Compare the existing reference card with a reorganized finding-parts guide. Four volunteers, V1 through V4, each performed two lookup tasks. Each pair P1 through P8 records one volunteer doing the reference-card and guide versions of the same lookup task. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent people. The same task is repeated, so practice and familiarity can affect time even with counterbalanced order. Order was balanced within each volunteer as recorded in pairs.csv. This was not a randomized sample of all store volunteers.

## Captured fields

reference.csv and guide.csv have pair_id,seconds,correct,assisted. Seconds is a positive elapsed time. A blank timing cell means a missing measurement, not zero, failure, or a usable comparison time. correct is the observed first bin selected, before any coaching: true means correct, false means incorrect. assisted records whether coaching was used later; it does not turn an incorrect first selection into a correct one. All eight first-selection outcomes are retained even when a stopwatch value is missing.

Use only pairs with both positive times for the time comparison. Match records by pair_id, not row position. Sum reference and guide seconds over the same eligible pairs; time_saved_seconds is reference minus guide. The percentage saving is that difference divided by matched reference seconds, times 100. Also count faster, slower and tied eligible pairs. Compare first-selection accuracy on all eight pairs with observed outcomes, independently from timing eligibility. Do not impute missing timing.

## Machine-readable audit

Write audit/metrics.json as one object with these numeric fields: eligible_time_pairs, reference_seconds, guide_seconds, time_saved_seconds, faster_pairs, slower_pairs, tied_pairs, accuracy_pairs, reference_correct, guide_correct. Use the recorded rules above. Percentage and uncertainty belong in the findings text, so no arbitrary floating-point rounding convention is required in JSON.

## Interpretation

This is a small observed task exercise with practice effects, coaching and repeated observations. It can inform a limited check. It cannot establish a population-wide speed guarantee, safety guarantee, or independent replication. Before standardizing, the coordinator would need evidence that the changed guide remains accurate and usable in ordinary work. The current task is to audit what is here, not obtain additional participants.
# Capture and observation notes

The session used local stopwatch sheets and first-selection cards. P7's guide stopwatch entry was lost during export; no other timing exists in this pack. Its guide first-selection card is retained and marked correct. Its later assistance flag is also retained. Do not reconstruct seconds from task order or another volunteer's record.

P3's reference first selection was wrong; P5's guide first selection was wrong. Observers later coached those tasks. The correct column describes the first selection and must not be rewritten to reflect eventual completion after help.

All records were collected in the same staffed exercise. Every volunteer tried both formats and repeated a lookup task. This supports a matched local description while leaving practice, staff assistance and ordinary-work transfer uncertain. No later unattended shift, expanded study or live rollout has occurred.

The draft summary was prepared before the missing-timing and first-selection notes were reconciled. It is historical input for correction, not a verified result.
# Unchecked summary for coordinator

The reorganized guide was tested on eight independent volunteers and all eight completed time pairs. It was faster in every pair and cut total lookup time by 30 percent. The guide had eight correct first selections out of eight, compared with seven for the reference card, so it also improved accuracy. Coaching did not affect any result.

These results establish that the guide should replace the reference card for every shift immediately. No further uncertainty affects that decision.

The underlying difficulty is that sending to the receiver and updating the stored job are separate operations. The rules provide no transaction that makes those two operations succeed or fail together.

A job’s stable `job_id` identifies the same job across attempts. Its state tracks the queue’s progress:

- **Ready:** a worker can claim it.
- **Leased:** a worker has claimed it for 30 seconds.
- **Done:** the queue considers its work complete.

The receiver has its own history: whether it accepted a notice. That history can disagree with the queue’s state. In particular, a notice can already be accepted while its job is still leased or available for retry.

The receiver has not received a notice from that attempt. The job remains unfinished. Once its lease expires, it becomes available to another worker, which can retry.

A stored job has a stable job_id and one state: ready, leased, or done.

This is a toy notification queue. Use only these rules.
A stored job has a stable job_id and one state: ready, leased, or done.
A worker leases a ready job for 30 seconds. A lease that expires before the job is done makes that job available to another worker.
A worker sends a notice to a separate receiver and then marks the stored job done. These are separate operations; there is no transaction spanning them.
A worker may stop at any point, and an old worker may continue running after its lease expires.
A send request may time out even if the receiver accepted it. The sender cannot infer acceptance from a timeout.
In the current design the receiver does not deduplicate requests.
We do not yet know whether the receiver can be changed to support durable idempotency keys.
Jobs can be retried. Eventual delivery requires that retries continue and some attempt eventually succeeds.
For this project a missed notice is worse than a duplicate, but duplicates should be prevented where the rules allow.
